newsitem.title: PERU: INTERVIEW-PERU'S YANACOCHA HITS RECORD GOLD OUTPUT.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-PERU'S YANACOCHA HITS RECORD GOLD OUTPUT.

text.p: Peru's largest gold miner, Minera Yanacocha S.A., registered its highest monthly production in July and projects a 25 percent rise in output throughout 1997, a senior company official said.
"In July we produced 92,000 ounces, which is a new record for us, so you can see our production is ramping upwards" Yanacocha general manager Thomas Conway told Reuters.

He added that Yanacocha, a joint venture run by Canada's Newmont Mining Corp and local Buenaventura in the northern Peruvian Andes, projects approximately one million ounces production throughout in 1997, up from 811,000 ounces last year.
He expected output to remain at that level for the next six or seven years. Yanacocha has already produced 485,000 ounces in the first half.
Conway stressed that although Yanaochoa was the largest gold-mine in South America, there were no major spending and investment plans for the medium-term.

"It obviously depends upon what the production profile is in Newmont and Buenaventura, and whether they wish to up production or hold it at a constant rate, so we have a lot of flexibility to do things," he said.
Conway added, however, that 1997 investments of $170 million was "the largest single year investment that we have ever made."
He said that small amounts of money invested would quickly be recouped by exports.

When asked about the current political instability in Peru and how it would affect investments, Conway said: "People that are going to invest a large sum of money need legal stability, so we would like to see a stable government ... The amount of money we invest is very small."

Conway indicated, however, that allegations of telephone- tapping by the secret services, the revocation of local nationality from Israeli-born businessman Baruch Ivcher followed by confiscation of his television station, and other local political crises, would probably not affect Yanacocha's investments.

The Yanacocha mining unit is located in the region of Cajamarca, some 540 miles (870 km) north-east of Lima. It was that region where the last Inca king sought unsuccesfully to buy his freedom from the Spanish colonizers by filling a room twice with gold and silver treasures.
